questions.question: You need a nightly script that saves screenshots of a few pages, with no test reports. Which package fits best?
options: `@playwright/test`, because it is the only one that can take screenshots
`playwright`, the automation library
`@axe-core/playwright`
`create-playwright`, run once per night
questions.explanation: The library gives you browser automation without a test runner, which is all a standalone script needs.

questions.question: After `npm install --save-dev @playwright/test`, a run says a browser executable doesn't exist. What is missing?
options: A `playwright.config.ts` file
The `--headed` flag
The browsers, installed with `npx playwright install`
A global install of the package
questions.explanation: The npm package doesn't include the browsers. `npx playwright install` downloads them.

questions.question: A config doesn't set `testDir`. Where does Playwright look for tests?
options: In the folder that holds the config file, including subfolders
Only in `./tests`
Only in `./e2e`
Nowhere, because `testDir` is required
questions.explanation: `testDir` defaults to the config file's folder. The `./tests` value you often see is written into the config by the init command.

questions.question: With the default settings, how do two tests in the same file run?
options: At the same time, in two workers
In random order, in one worker
In two separate browser contexts that share cookies
In order, in the same worker
questions.explanation: Files run in parallel by default, but tests in one file stay in order in one worker unless `fullyParallel` is on.

questions.question: Why might a `test.beforeAll` hook run several times in one test run?
options: It runs before every test in the file
It runs once per worker, and a failed test restarts the worker
It runs once per assertion
It retries until the hook times out
questions.explanation: Each worker runs the hook for itself. A new worker replaces one that hit a failure, so the hook runs again there.
